blocks.text: The AI Assets Models page in AI Security Admin Portal is a centralized model inventory that provides a unified view of all custom, managed, and unmanaged models across your environments, enabling standardized governance through clear classification and sanctioning. By surfacing benchmark-based risk signals and sensitive data exposure indicators, it allows teams to prioritize remediation and make informed data protection decisions. This shared visibility streamlines investigation and triage via granular search and filters, ensuring that security, governance, and engineering teams remain aligned on approved models and operational actions.
The AI Assets - Models Page provides the following benefits and enables you to:

blocks.item: Maintain an inventory of detected LLMs across the enterprise, including foundation models, custom (fine-tuned) models, and unmanaged or open-source models, e.g., Hugging Face or Ollama.
See where each model was discovered, when it was last discovered and updated, and its associated risk and security signals.
Classify models as assets and apply a governance status, e.g., Sanctioned, Unsanctioned, or Pending, where supported.
Prioritize review and remediation using benchmark-based model risk signals and, when available, supply-chain risk.
Identify sensitive data exposure by viewing DLP indicators, e.g., top classified data types and engines associated with model usage.
Provide shared visibility so security, governance, and engineering teams can align on approved models, exceptions, and next steps as the model landscape changes.

blocks.heading: About the AI Assets - Models Page

blocks.text: On the AI Assets Models page (AI Infrastructure > AI Assets - Models), you can do the following:

blocks.item: Filter by Business Units.
View metrics from the following perspectives:

Models by Risk: View distribution of the model's vulnerability to adversarial exploits, such as prompt injection, jailbreaking, and unauthorized data extraction. Ratings are categorized as Critical, High, Medium, or Low. This score specifically measures the model's attack resistance rather than the severity of known open issues.
Models by Status: View the distribution of governance status of each model, categorized as Sanctioned, Unsanctioned, or Pending.
Models by Subtype: View the distribution of the model's origin. The categories are as follows:
Foundation: A vendor-provided, pre-trained base model, e.g., an LLM or embedding model and used as-is.
Free-Tuning: A foundation model trained further on your organization’s data for specific tasks.
Imported: A model introduced from an external source, e.g., third-party model registry, open-source repository, or another account or tenant.
Unknown: The subtype could not be determined from the available metadata.
Others: Models that do not match the listed subtypes.
Search for a specific model.
Click Export to export the data and download the report as an Excel file.
Show or Hide columns.
Show or Hide filters.
Apply filters
Environment: Returns data about the environment where the AI model was discovered based on your filter selections, such as AWS, Azure, or GCP.
Type: Returns data about the category of the AI model based on your filter selections. The following options are supported:
Managed: AI models that are fully managed by a cloud service provider (CSP), such as AWS Bedrock or Azure OpenAI.
Unmanaged: AI models that are deployed and managed independently, outside a CSP's managed offering.
Custom: AI models that are built and trained in-house by the organization.
Registry Model: AI models that are sourced from a model registry or public repository, such as Hugging Face or a container registry.
Subtype: Returns data about the specific classification within the model type based on your filter selections, providing a more granular view of the model's function or architecture.

Source: Returns data about the origin of the AI model based on your filter selections, such as whether it was built in-house, sourced from a third-party provider, or obtained from a public model repository.
Status: Returns data about the current operational state of the AI model based on your filter selections, such as whether it is pending, sanctioned, or unsanctioned.

Sensitive Data: Returns data about whether the AI model has access to or processes sensitive data based on your filter selections, as detected by DLP engines or document types, such as personally identifiable information (PII), financial data, or health records.

Model Risk: Model Risk Indicates the risk level associated with the AI model based on factors such as known vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, or non-compliance with security policies. The following risk levels are supported:
Critical: The model has severe vulnerabilities or misconfigurations that require immediate attention.
High: The model has significant vulnerabilities or misconfigurations that pose a considerable security risk.
Medium: The model has moderate vulnerabilities or misconfigurations that should be addressed in a timely manner.
Low: The model has minor vulnerabilities or misconfigurations that present a minimal security risk.
Unknown: The risk level of the model could not be determined due to insufficient data or incomplete scanning.
Model Supply Chain Risk: Returns data about the risk associated with the AI model's supply chain, including the libraries, dependencies, and third-party components used to build or run the model.

View a list of AI models that were discovered. For each AI model you can view:
Name: The name of the AI model. Click the model name to view additional details.
General Information: Information such as region, environment, type, subtype, account ID, and account name. Click More Details to view a graphical summary.

Model Score: Risk of the model being exploited through adversarial attacks like prompt injection, jaikbreaks, and data extraction. Benchmark-based risk score is shown only when a benchmark has been run. If the model type is unmanaged and if the risk score is greater than 0, another tab, Model Security, is visible. To view further details, click View Model Benchmark.
Lifecycle: Timeline of key milestones from discovery to deployment, monitoring, and updates.
The detailed information page also displays the following tabs:
Graph View

The graphs consist of interactive nodes that provide contextual information, e.g., cloud account name, region, type, account ID, account name, file path, risk score, about the primary AI model and the associated secondary resources.

The graphs also include attack paths that show how the resource is compromised either through public exposure, malware, by an IAM entity (user, service, role) with access privileges, vulnerabilities, etc. This information helps you analyze the issues in detail and remediate them immediately.
Click the nodes to view additional details of each entity.
Issues
View a list of issues that were discovered. For each issue, you can view:
Issue ID: The unique identifier for the issue.
Policy Name: The policy title.
Policy Category: The threat category, e.g., public exposure, data loss, etc., that the policy belongs to.
Risk Level: The risk level, i.e., Critical, High, Medium, or Low.
Cloud Account: The unique identifier of the cloud account in which the model is located.
Created On: The date and time the issue was created.
Last Updated: The date and time the issue was last updated.
Model Supply Chain Risk
The risk assessment results for an unmanaged AI model summarize the risk assessment across the following categories:
Risk Score: Indicates the composite supply chain risk for this model on a scale of 0 to 100.
Severity: Indicates the severity category, i.e., Critical, High, Medium, or Low derived by rolling up the underlying numeric risk score.
Documentation: Checks the license type and library framework of the AI model.
Risk Indicators: Evaluates the AI model for specific risks like unsafe files or missing Safetensors file formats.

Files: Analyzes the AI model file formats and security scan results (scanned by Hugging Face) to check for Safetensors file formats, config.json, and README. Unsafe, Caution, and Suspicious labels are assigned to suspicious files.
Model Security (Only for unmanaged models)
You can view model security details in the following sections:
Performance Summary: Indicates the benchmark results across four quality dimensions, i.e., Security, Safety, Hallucinations, and Business Alignment.
You can also view details in the following tabs:
Overall
No System Prompt
Basic System Prompt
Hardened System Prompt
Test Results Drilldown: You can view the overall probe cards displaying the cumulative scores of the model.
Compare: Click the Compare tab and select the models you want to review to evaluate several models for your use case.
The comparison view shows side-by-side performance across multiple categories and system prompt configurations, so you can quickly choose the best option. To learn more, see About Model Security.
Usage (Only for AWS managed and custom models)
View a timeline showing the usage activity of the AI model over time. The following details are available in the table:
Invoker Principal: The principal entity, such as a user, role, or service account, that invoked the AI model.
Invoker User Name: The username associated with the entity that invoked the AI model.
Last Seen: The most recent date and time the AI model was invoked or detected.
Invocation Count: The total number of times the AI model has been invoked.
Top 10 Users (Only for AWS managed and custom models)
View a list of the top 10 invokers associated with the AI model. For each invoker, the following details are available:
Invoker Principal: The principal entity, such as a user, role, or service account, that invoked the AI model.
Invoker User Name: The username associated with the entity that invoked the AI model.
Last Seen: The most recent date and time the AI model was invoked or detected.
Invocation Count: The total number of times the AI model has been invoked.
Type & Subtype: The AI model type, e.g., Managed Model, Unmanaged Model, Custom Model, etc. and the model subtype, e.g., Fine-tuning.
Environment: Indicates where the asset was discovered, e.g., AWS, Azure, GCP, etc.
Source: Indicates the specific location or service where the AI model was discovered, stored, or hosted.
Status: The model's governance status, e.g., Pending, Sanctioned, or Unsanctioned.
Sensitive Data: The DLP engines used for classification and the document types detected in model-related data.
Model Risk: The model's benchmark-based average risk score, e.g., Critical, High, Medium, Low, or Unknown.
Model Supply Chain Risk: The severity rating from supply chain analysis, e.g., Critical, High, Medium, Low, or Unknown.
